articles.title: Quick start: set up Velstrian Tenderworks for your first tender
articles.summary: Set up your company details, add the documents that prove what you do, and start your first bid for a public or private buyer.
articles.html:
Who this is for

This guide is for anyone writing a bid, including a small business with no bid team. It works the same whether you are bidding for public sector work (a local authority, an NHS trust, a government department) or for a private company’s tender or request for a quote. Follow the five steps below and your company details, your evidence and your first bid are ready for real work.

The five steps at a glance

  1. Organisation profile: legal details and accreditations.
  2. Evidence Vault setup: policies, ISO certificates and case studies.
  3. Bid workspace: upload the buyer’s documents, for example the invitation to tender (ITT) and the specification.
  4. Drafting and scoring: answers that cite your own documents. On public sector bids, social value answers are also scored against PPN 026, the government’s social value rules.
  5. Export the submission: Word, PDF and the compliance matrix.

Step 1: Configure your organisation profile

  1. Navigate to Settings > Organisation.
  2. Confirm your registered legal name, Companies House number, trading name, and primary domain.
  3. Specify your operational sectors (e.g. Facilities Management, Construction, IT Services) and UK regional coverage.
  4. Click Save profile. Velstrian Bid embeds these facts into answer contexts to avoid hallucinated company parameters.

Step 2: Seed the Evidence Vault

Upload the documents buyers usually ask to see, in public and private tenders alike. Public buyers often ask for them in a selection questionnaire (SQ), the first set of questions about your company:

  • Certifications: ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials Plus.
  • Insurance: Employer Liability (£10m), Public Liability (£5m), Professional Indemnity.
  • Mandatory Policies: Modern Slavery Statement, Health & Safety, Equality & Diversity, Whistleblowing.
  • Carbon Reduction Plan (PPN 006): your baseline emissions and yearly reduction targets. Public buyers ask for it on larger contracts, and many private buyers ask too.
Only upload current, approved versions. Buyers check expiry dates and who signed each policy.

Step 3: Choose your workspace

  • Velstrian Bid: for suppliers. Read the buyer’s documents, list every requirement in a compliance matrix, plan your social value commitments and draft answers that cite your evidence.
  • Velstrian Buy: for buyers, public or private. Set out what you need, score the bids suppliers send and agree the final scores with colleagues.
  • Settings: your team, what each person can do, the audit log and billing.

articles.title: End-to-end bid management workflow in Velstrian Bid
articles.summary: Every step of a bid in plain words, from adding the buyer's documents to sending your answers and recording the result.
articles.html:
Who this is for

Anyone running a bid in Velstrian Bid, including a small business with no bid team. It works the same for a public sector tender and for a private company’s request for a quote. This guide shows the whole journey once, so you know what comes next at every step.

The bid at a glance

Every bid has an Overview and four stages, shown across the top of the bid in three milestones: Tender and strategy, Response and evidence, and Review and sign off.

  1. Tender. Add the buyer’s documents. Velstrian Bid reads them and suggests the requirements, word for word from the tender. You confirm each one. On a public bid this stage also holds Social value, and the selection questionnaire when the tender has one.
  2. Response. Answer each question. Draft with AI writes a first draft from your own documents and past answers and shows the sources it used. You edit it and save it.
  3. Sign-off. A colleague reviews the bid and records a verdict. Your organisation decides the review gates, and the bid moves on only when each gate is passed.
  4. Submit and outcome. Download your answers, send them through the buyer’s portal or by email yourself, then record that you submitted and, later, whether you won.

Step by step

  1. Choose Start a bid, drop the tender documents, say who you are bidding to (public or private) and give the bid a name.
  2. On Tender, open Requirements and confirm, edit or reject each suggested requirement. Only confirmed requirements count in the compliance matrix.
  3. On Response, draft and save every answer.
  4. On Sign-off, ask a reviewer to read the bid and record their verdict.
  5. Use Export at the top of any bid screen to download your response.

What happens next

Velstrian Bid never sends anything to a buyer. When you have submitted, record it on Submit and outcome. When the buyer tells you the result, mark the bid won or lost and keep their letter, so the next bid can learn from it.

Common problems

  • A requirement is missing. Add it by hand on Requirements, or check whether a scanned page could not be read.
  • The export is marked as a draft. Something is still missing. The export panel lists what, so finish those items first.

articles.title: Procurement Act 2023: compliance & transparency notices guide
articles.summary: The main changes the Procurement Act 2023 brought for public buyers and the suppliers who bid to them, and where Velstrian Tenderworks helps.
articles.html:
What the Act is

The Procurement Act 2023 sets the rules public bodies follow when they buy goods, services and works. It came into force on 24 February 2025 and replaced the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and related regulations in England, Wales and Northern Ireland. Scottish devolved bodies follow their own rules. It does not apply to private companies buying for themselves. If you only sell to private buyers, their own invitation and contract set the rules.

Key changes

Area Before (PCR 2015) Procurement Act 2023
How the winner is chosen Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT) Most Advantageous Tender (MAT), which lets buyers weigh wider benefits such as social value alongside price.
Notices Contract award notices Notices on a central digital platform across planning, tender, award and contract performance.
Performance Managed privately Contracts above £5 million set at least three key performance indicators (KPIs) and publish how the supplier performs against them.
Feedback to bidders Letters in no fixed form An assessment summary for every bidder before the standstill period begins.

What it means for a small supplier

  • Public opportunities under the Act are published on Find a Tender.
  • Expect the buyer to explain your scores in an assessment summary. Read it, because it shows where you lost marks.
  • After an award, the buyer waits a standstill period of 8 working days before entering the contract.

Where Velstrian Tenderworks helps

  • Velstrian Bid: paste a Find a Tender or Contracts Finder notice link on Start a bid and the buyer, value, deadline and procedure are read for you to confirm.
  • Velstrian Buy: the requirement builder shows which side of the Act’s threshold a purchase falls, the contracts list shows when the mandatory standstill ends, and an evaluation can prepare a draft assessment summary for each bidder, which you check and approve before sending. Drafts are not legal advice.

articles.title: Create and structure a Velstrian Bid tender workspace
articles.summary: Add the contract you are bidding for, public or private, set how it will be scored, and get one tidy place for the bid.
articles.html:
Why workspaces matter

A Velstrian Bid workspace keeps everything for one bid in one place: the documents, the requirements, who is working on it, the AI credits used and a record of every change. One workspace per bid keeps each buyer’s documents, and the evidence you cite for them, separate. It works the same for a public sector tender and for a private buyer’s request for a quote.

Step 1: Enter opportunity details

  1. Click Velstrian Bid > Start a bid.
  2. Bid name: use the title the buyer uses. Public contracts are listed on Find a Tender or Contracts Finder. For a private buyer, use the title on its invitation or request for a quote.
  3. Who you are bidding to: on a public bid this is the Contracting authority, for example Crown Commercial Service, an NHS trust or a local authority. On a private bid it is the Buyer organisation, the company asking for bids.
  4. Contract value: the estimated total value of the contract. On public bids it decides which social value rules apply.
  5. Submission deadline: the exact date and time. It appears in your compliance calendar so you do not miss it.

Step 2: Set evaluation weightings

Buyers say how they will score bids, usually as a split between quality and price. Copy the split from the buyer’s documents:

  • Quality / Technical weighting: Typically 50% to 70%.
  • Commercial / Price weighting: Typically 20% to 40%.
  • Social Value weighting: enter the weighting the buyer gives social value, if any. Private buyers set their own. PPN 026 states a minimum of 10% for contracts valued at 1m GBP and above but less than 5m GBP, and 20% at 5m GBP or above, for central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies on procurements commenced on or after 1 January 2027. Velstrian Bid warns when the weighting you enter is under that figure and never blocks the entry. Other contracting authorities are not bound by it and may weight social value at whatever figure their notice states.

Step 3: Initialise workspace

Click Create workspace. You then upload the buyer’s documents and Velstrian Bid lists what they ask for.

articles.title: Upload, parse and organise procurement documents
articles.summary: Add the buyer's tender documents to a bid, check that each one was read, and confirm the requirements found in them.
articles.html:
What this step is for

The buyer’s documents tell you what they want and how they will score it. When you add them to a bid, Velstrian Bid reads the text and suggests the requirements, so you start from a full list instead of reading every page with a highlighter. This works for a public sector invitation to tender (ITT) and for a private buyer’s request for a proposal or a quote.

Which files to add

Add everything the buyer sent: the instructions, the specification, the question or response template, the pricing schedule and any clarifications. The upload box accepts: ZIP pack, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, CSV or TXT · up to 100 MB each. A ZIP pack is opened for you, and you see what is inside before anything uploads.

Each file gets a document type, such as Invitation to tender (ITT), Specification, Pricing schedule, Response template or Addendum or clarification. The type is suggested from the file name. Change it if it is wrong.

Step by step

  1. Open the bid and go to Tender.
  2. Drop the files on the upload box, or choose them. Before the upload, Velstrian Bid tells you about how many AI credits reading them will use.
  3. Watch the Extraction column. Text ready means the file was read.
  4. Choose Suggest requirements, then Review requirements.
  5. Confirm, edit or reject each suggestion. Suggestions that quote the tender word for word can be confirmed together.

What happens next

Confirmed requirements appear in the compliance matrix, where you give each one an owner and link it to an answer. If the buyer issues a new version of a document, upload it and say which earlier file it replaces, so the change can be compared.

Common problems

  • Needs OCR. The file is a scanned image, so its text could not be read. Upload a text based version, or add the requirements by hand.
  • Partially extracted. Some scanned pages could not be read, so requirements from those pages may be missing. Check them against the tender.
  • Locked PDF. Remove the password, then upload it again. No credits are used on a locked file.

articles.title: Build an audit-proof compliance matrix before drafting
articles.summary: Make one list of everything the buyer asks for, give each item an owner, and track whether it is answered.
articles.html:
What a compliance matrix is

A compliance matrix is a checklist of everything the buyer asks for, with who is answering each item and whether it is done. Missing one requirement can cost marks, and on a public tender a missed pass or fail item can rule a bid out. The matrix makes the gaps visible before you submit, for public and private bids alike.

Step 1: confirm the requirements

  1. Upload the tender documents on Tender and choose Suggest requirements.
  2. Open Requirements. Each suggestion quotes the tender word for word.
  3. Confirm, edit or reject each one. Use the filters To review, Confirmed and Rejected to work through the list.
  4. Add anything the reader missed with Add requirement. If the buyer sent a spreadsheet of requirements, use Import a requirements matrix instead.

Only requirements you confirm are counted. Rejected ones are left out.

Step 2: track each requirement

The Compliance matrix view lists every confirmed requirement with these columns:

  • Requirement: the buyer’s own words.
  • Response status: Not started, Draft, Covered or Gap.
  • Owner: the team member answering it.
  • Linked answer: the answer on the Response stage that covers it.
  • Notes: anything the team needs to know.

You own the matrix. AI suggests the requirements, and you decide the response, the owner and the status.

What happens next

Draft the linked answers on Response and move each row to Covered when it is answered. You can download the whole list with Download the full requirement pack (CSV) to share it. On a public bid where a Carbon Reduction Plan applies, the same screen shows what the plan still needs.

Common problems

  • The matrix is empty. No requirement is confirmed yet. Review the suggestions first.
  • We may have missed some requirements. This warning appears when parts of a document produced none. Check those parts, or ask for the document to be read again.

articles.title: Generate, cite and edit winning bid narratives
articles.summary: Draft each answer with AI from your own documents and past answers, check the sources it used, then edit it in your own words.
articles.html:
What this is for

Writing answers is the longest part of a bid. Velstrian Bid writes a first draft of each answer from the buyer’s question, your evidence vault and your answer library, and shows which source backs which words. You stay the author: you check the draft, change what is wrong and save the version you want to send.

Step by step

  1. Open the bid and go to Response.
  2. Pick a question. The editor shows the word limit the tender states, or says that none is stated.
  3. Choose Draft with AI. Velstrian Bid writes the draft from your own sources.
  4. Read the draft under AI draft. Review before use. A numbered mark shows which source backs those words. Open one to read the source’s own wording.
  5. Choose Use this draft, edit it in your own words, then choose Save answer.
  6. If the answer is a good one, choose Save to answer library so the next bid can reuse it.

Make the draft sound like you

In Brand voice you choose how answers sound, for example friendly or formal, and British or American spelling. It changes the wording only, never the facts or figures.

Writing tips

  • Answer the question asked. Cover every part of it, in the order the buyer asks.
  • Prove each claim. Replace “we are the leading provider” with something you can show, such as a contract you delivered and what it achieved.
  • Say how. Explain who does the work, with what, and how you will check it is done well.

What happens next

Each save is kept as a version, so you can compare versions and go back. When every answer is written, review the bid on the Sign-off stage.

Common problems

  • The draft cannot be used. It stated a figure that is not in your commitments or official data. Draft it again, or write that part yourself.
  • Nothing in your answer library was close enough. The draft is written from the requirement alone. Add evidence and past answers, then draft again.
  • AI drafting is not available. Your answer is untouched. Try again later or write it yourself.

articles.title: Collaborative review, team assignments & sign-off gates
articles.summary: Ask colleagues and outside reviewers to check a bid, record each review verdict, and release the bid to submit.
articles.html:
Why review a bid

A second pair of eyes catches the question you did not fully answer and the claim you cannot prove. Velstrian Bid gives every bid a review ladder, so each check happens in order and nothing is sent before someone with authority has signed it off.

The review stages

The built in ladder uses three colour teams:

  • Pink team: read the outline of each answer and say whether it answers the question and covers what the buyer asks for.
  • Red team: score each answer against the question and say what would lose marks.
  • Gold team: a final read before submission. A Gold sign off releases the bid to submit, and only an admin or owner can record it.

Your organisation can rename the gates, change their order, add one or archive one in Velstrian Bid settings, under Review gates. Sign offs already recorded keep the name they were signed under.

Step by step

  1. Open the bid and go to Sign-off.
  2. The reviewer reads the answers, then chooses a verdict, adds comments and records the sign off.
  3. A pass moves the bid to the next gate. To send it back, choose an earlier stage and give a reason.
  4. Review help can mark an answer against each of the buyer’s scoring points with a second AI model. It only suggests. The reviewer sets the mark.

Who can do what

  • A Viewer reads everything, comments on answers and records an approve, changes requested or reject decision.
  • An External reviewer is someone outside your organisation you invite by email. Their access lasts the number of days you choose, covers this one bid, and is read and comment only. A guest can never sign off. You can revoke it at any time.

What happens next

When the last gate passes, the bid is released to submit. Nothing is sent to the buyer. You submit through the buyer’s portal or channel and record it on Submit and outcome.

Common problems

  • You cannot record the Gold sign off. Ask an admin or the owner.
  • Review settings are locked. Bid review and external reviewers are part of a paid Velstrian Bid plan.

articles.title: Exporting submission packs (Word, PDF, Excel Matrix, Audit ZIP)
articles.summary: Download your answers in the buyer's own template, or as Word, PDF, PowerPoint, Excel or a whole pack, ready to send.
articles.html:
What this is for

When your answers are ready you need them in the format the buyer asked for. Velstrian Bid can write your answers into the buyer’s own document, or build a separate proposal pack. Exporting never submits anything. You send the files through the buyer’s portal or by email yourself.

Where to find it

Choose Export at the top of any screen in the bid. It opens the Export your response panel. Every screen opens the same panel, so there is only one place to look.

Your choices

  • In the buyer’s own template (recommended). If you uploaded the buyer’s Word or Excel response document, your answers are written into its own response cells. Check first: anything that cannot be placed is listed by name, so you can add it by hand.
  • Other formats. The proposal pack as Word (.docx), PDF (tagged for accessibility), PowerPoint (.pptx) or Excel (.xlsx), or the whole pack as a .zip file.
  • Buyer portal files. On Submit and outcome, pick the buyer’s portal and download your approved answers as CSV or Excel to load into it. Only answers a person approved are in the file.

Step by step

  1. Make sure every answer is saved and reviewed.
  2. Choose Export and read the notice at the top of the panel.
  3. Choose the buyer’s template or another format and download it.
  4. Open the file and check it before you send it.

What happens next

Submit the files in the buyer’s portal or channel. Then, on Submit and outcome, choose I have submitted in the portal, add the portal’s confirmation number if it gave one, and later record whether you won.

Common problems

  • Every export is marked as a draft. Something is still missing. The panel lists what, so finish those items and export again.
  • No buyer template option. No Word or Excel tender document is uploaded. Upload it on Tender, or use the proposal pack.

articles.title: How social value scoring & TOMs proxy calculations work
articles.summary: How the social value you promise is given a pound value, for public and private bids, and the minimum weightings PPN 026 sets for public contracts.
articles.html:
How TOMs scoring works

Social value is the extra good your contract does, such as jobs, apprenticeships or spending with local suppliers. UK public sector buyers score it, and many private buyers ask for it too. TOMs (Themes, Outcomes and Measures) is a common way to list those promises so each one can be given a pound value. Velstrian Bid values each promise with the Oxford Social Value Bank proxy values held in the measure library, so the same promise always produces the same figure.

Calculation formula

Total Social Value (£) = ∑ (Measure Proxy Value × Committed Quantity × Duration Factor)

Example measures

The proxy value per unit is held against each measure in the library and shown beside it when you enter a quantity. These are four of the measures Velstrian Bid offers.

Measure code Measure description Unit
JOB_LT_UNEMPLOYED Long-term unemployed person into employment Per person per year
APPRENTICESHIP_12M Apprenticeship created (12+ months) Per apprenticeship
LOCAL_SUPPLY_CHAIN Local SME supply-chain spend Per £100 local spend
VOLUNTEER_HOUR_SKILLED Skilled volunteer hour Per hour

What the summary shows on a PPN 026 contract

Velstrian Bid builds every new contract against PPN 026. The summary reports your committed proxy value and its share of the declared contract value, with no pass or fail colour, because PPN 026 states a minimum social value weighting in the evaluation and sets no target for committed proxy value.

PPN 026 states a minimum weighting of 10% for contracts valued at 1m GBP and above but less than 5m GBP, and 20% at 5m GBP or above, for the central government bodies it addresses on procurements commenced on or after 1 January 2027. It states no minimum below 1m GBP. You record the weighting and the award criteria the notice names in the contract wizard.

articles.title: PPN 06/20 social value themes & Model Award Criteria (superseded)
articles.summary: The five social value themes and Model Award Criteria introduced by PPN 06/20. PPN 06/20 was superseded for procurements commencing on or after 24 February 2025, so this article is a reference for contracts recorded under it.
articles.html:
PPN 06/20 has been superseded. It ceased to apply to procurements commencing on or after 24 February 2025. This article is a reference for contracts recorded under it. Velstrian Bid builds every new contract against PPN 026, and a contract already recorded under PPN 06/20 stays readable and exportable and keeps naming PPN 06/20.

The Social Value Model as PPN 06/20 defined it

Procurement Policy Note 06/20 asked central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies to evaluate social value with a minimum 10 percent weighting in tender awards. It structured the model into five national priority themes. A PPN is a Cabinet Office instruction addressed to those bodies rather than law, so PPN 06/20 never bound local authorities, NHS bodies or universities.

The 5 national social value themes under PPN 06/20

Theme Focus area Typical buyer objectives
Theme 1: Fighting climate change Environmental sustainability & net zero Carbon Reduction Plans (now PPN 006), waste minimisation, circular economy commitments and biodiversity protection.
Theme 2: Tackling economic inequality Supply chain resilience & skills SME and VCSE supply chain spend, local employment, apprenticeships, digital skills training and prompt payment codes.
Theme 3: Covid-19 recovery / resilient communities Community resilience Physical and mental health support, local community projects, workplace safety and remote collaboration support.
Theme 4: Equal opportunity Fair work & inclusion Reducing disability employment gap, pay equality, inclusive hiring, modern slavery risk management and fair living wage commitments.
Theme 5: Wellbeing Health & community wellbeing Staff wellbeing charters, mental health first aiders, community integration and public health partnerships.

Model Award Criteria (MACs)

A PPN 06/20 tender named one or more Model Award Criteria, for example MAC 1.1 or MAC 2.2, under the theme it belonged to. Velstrian Bid does not map questions to MAC numbers. A contract recorded under PPN 06/20 keeps the theme codes T1 to T5 it was built with.

What Velstrian Bid uses for new contracts

PPN 026, published 5 August 2026, applies to central government procurements commenced on or after 1 January 2027 and valued at 1m GBP or more including VAT. Its model has two outcomes, Good jobs and Skills, across six award criteria. It states a minimum social value weighting of 10% from 1m GBP and 20% from 5m GBP.

Velstrian Bid builds every new contract against PPN 026. In the contract wizard you select the award criteria the contract notice names. Velstrian Bid does not rank the six criteria or choose them for you, because PPN 026 publishes no ordering.

Structuring a high-scoring response

  1. Method Statement: Explain how you will deliver the commitment during contract performance.
  2. Quantitative Metrics: Provide exact numbers (e.g. 5 apprenticeships, £50k local supply chain spend, 25% carbon reduction).
  3. Monitoring & Governance: Name the role responsible for reporting progress to the contract manager.
  4. Evidence Base: Cite historical delivery data or accredited policies from your Evidence Vault.
Vague intentions score low. Evaluators look for commitments that are contractual, measurable and tied directly to the contract delivery location.

articles.title: Oxford Social Value Bank proxy methodology
articles.summary: How Velstrian Bid puts a pound value on the social value you promise, and how to choose promises you can keep.
articles.html:
What a proxy value is

Social value is the extra good a contract does, such as jobs for local people, apprenticeships or spending with small local suppliers. Public buyers score it, and many private buyers ask for it too. A proxy value is an agreed pound figure for one unit of an outcome, for example one apprenticeship. Velstrian Bid uses the Oxford Social Value Bank proxy values, which put a monetary figure on a social or economic outcome using cost benefit analysis and wellbeing valuation. Every figure the product reports is that proxy value multiplied by the quantity you commit, so it is computed rather than estimated.

Principles to follow

  • Additionality: count only good that happens because of this contract. Business as usual activities do not count.
  • Deadweight: outcomes that would have happened anyway are taken out.
  • Attribution: claim only your own share of an outcome you deliver with others.

Step by step

On a public bid, open Social value on the Tender stage. It has three steps:

  1. What the buyer asks: confirm the criteria and the weighting the buyer set.
  2. What you commit: choose the measures you will deliver and enter a quantity for each. The table shows each measure’s proxy value and the social value it adds. Suggest measures can propose some for you to check.
  3. How it scores: the score and the theme coverage of what you committed.

Your commitments are saved automatically.

Choosing the right measures

Read the buyer’s specification to see whether they care most about local jobs, local spending or cutting carbon, and match your commitments to their stated local plan. Map each commitment to the wording the buyer’s own notice uses rather than a bare theme number. Only promise what you can deliver and evidence, because the buyer can measure you against it after award.

Common problems

  • No share of contract value is shown. The contract value is not recorded on the bid. Record it to see the share.
  • No contract term is recorded. A measure priced by the year is then counted for 12 months. Record the term to get the right figure.

articles.title: Carbon Reduction Plans (PPN 006) & Net Zero commitments
articles.summary: What a Carbon Reduction Plan is, when a public buyer asks for one under PPN 006, and how to prepare it in Velstrian Bid. PPN 006 replaced PPN 06/21.
articles.html:
What a Carbon Reduction Plan is

A Carbon Reduction Plan (CRP) is a short public document that says how much carbon your business produces, your target for reaching net zero and what you are doing to get there. Some public buyers require one before you can win a contract, and many private buyers now ask for the same information.

When it is required (PPN 006)

PPN 006, Taking account of Carbon Reduction Plans in the procurement of major government contracts, requires bidders for contracts with an estimated value above £5 million per year including VAT to publish a compliant Carbon Reduction Plan detailing Scope 1, Scope 2, and a defined subset of Scope 3 emissions. It is addressed to central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies, and applies to relevant procurements advertised on or after 24 February 2025. It replaced PPN 06/21, which carried the same duty under the old numbering.

The NHS requirement is broader. Under the NHS net zero supplier roadmap a Carbon Reduction Plan is required for all new NHS procurements, with no value threshold at all since April 2024.

What a plan contains

Section Required data
Baseline emissions Your footprint in a baseline year (tCO2e) across Scope 1, Scope 2 and the required Scope 3 categories.
Current emissions Emissions in your most recent reporting year.
Reduction target Your commitment to reach net zero by 2050 at the latest.
Carbon reduction projects Measures you have completed and measures you have planned.
Sign off A director signs the plan, and it is reviewed every year.

How to prepare it in Velstrian Bid

  1. Open Bid profile in Velstrian Bid settings. Under Baseline, net zero target and carbon reduction projects, record your baseline year, target year and the footprint you commit to reaching. Velstrian Bid never guesses any of these.
  2. Add each carbon reduction project in your own words, marked Completed or Planned. If you state a saving, name the record it comes from, because a buyer can hold you to it.
  3. On a bid where PPN 006 applies, the Carbon Reduction Plan panel on the compliance matrix lists anything still missing. Choose Generate from recorded emissions, then download the plan as Word or PDF.
  4. Upload the signed plan to your evidence vault so later bids can use it.

Common problems

  • No emissions measured yet. The plan cannot show zero for a footprint nobody measured. Record your emissions first.
  • The panel does not appear. PPN 006 does not apply to this bid, for example a private bid or a contract below the threshold.

articles.title: Evidence Vault: managing policies, accreditations & case studies
articles.summary: Keep your certificates, policies, insurance and case studies in one place, with their expiry dates, so every bid can use them.
articles.html:
What the evidence vault is for

Buyers ask for proof: certificates, policies, insurance and examples of work you have done. Public buyers often ask for them in a selection questionnaire (SQ), the first set of questions about your company, and private buyers ask for the same kind of proof. The evidence vault keeps every one of these documents in one place, so you upload each file once and every bid can use it. Velstrian Bid also reads the vault when it drafts answers, so an answer can point to a real document.

What to upload

  • Certificates and accreditations: for example ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 27001, Cyber Essentials, CHAS or Constructionline.
  • Policies: health and safety, environmental, modern slavery, safeguarding, equality and anti bribery.
  • Insurance and finance: insurance schedules and your latest accounts.
  • Case studies: short write ups of contracts you delivered, with what you achieved.

Step by step

  1. Open Evidence from the main menu.
  2. Drop your files on Upload evidence. The box says how many files you can add at a time.
  3. Velstrian Tenderworks reads each file for its type, issuer and expiry date, and quotes the words it read them from. Choose Accept, Correct or Reject for each suggestion.
  4. Check that every certificate has the right expiry date.

Keeping it up to date

Each file shows a status: Fresh, Expiring when its expiry date is within 30 days, Stale once it has passed, or No expiry. Filter by Expiring once a month and upload the renewed certificate before the old one runs out. Buyers check expiry dates and who signed each policy, so only upload current, approved versions.

What happens next

When you open the vault from a bid, it shows which files may cover that bid’s open requirements. A file that satisfies more than one requirement is marked Reused, so you can see which documents matter most.

Common problems

  • We could not read this file. Its details are unchanged. Set the type and expiry date yourself.
  • You cannot upload. Only a colleague who can edit can add evidence. You can still open and download what is there.

articles.title: Verifiable proof & automated citation mapping in answers
articles.summary: How Velstrian Bid shows which of your documents backs each part of a drafted answer, so you can check it before you send it.
articles.html:
Why sources matter

A buyer can hold you to anything you write in a bid. If an answer says you hold a certificate or delivered a result, you need the document that proves it. Velstrian Bid keeps a link between each drafted answer and the sources it was written from, so you can check every claim before the bid goes out. This matters as much for a private buyer as for a public one.

Where the sources come from

  • Your document: a file in your evidence vault.
  • Your answer library: an answer you saved from an earlier bid.
  • Tender document or Tender clause: the buyer’s own words.
  • Regulatory source: published rules and guidance.

How to check a draft

  1. On Response, open a question and choose Draft with AI.
  2. In the draft, a numbered mark shows which source backs those words. Open the mark to read the source’s own wording.
  3. Open How this answer was made to see how many documents were read, which parts were used, how many of the buyer’s points the answer covers and how many of its claims are backed.
  4. Read the Credentials to confirm list. It names any certificate or accreditation the draft mentions that your company record does not show, or that your record says has expired.

What happens next

Fix or remove any claim you cannot prove, then save the answer. If a certificate has expired, upload the renewed one to the evidence vault before you submit.

Common problems

  • Two of your answers give different figures. The library answers used for this draft disagree. Decide which figure is right and correct the other answer.
  • This source was recorded without a quotable passage. There is no wording to show. Open the document itself to check it.
  • No trail for this older answer. Answers written before the trail existed do not have one.

articles.title: Check suppliers before and after award
articles.summary: Keep a directory of the suppliers you buy from, see what the public company register says about each one, and record what you find.
articles.html:
What this is for

Before you award a contract you want to know the supplier is a real, active company. After award you want a record of how they performed. Velstrian Buy keeps both in the supplier record, for public bodies and for private companies buying for themselves. It never decides for you: every check is there for you to read and judge.

Step by step

  1. Open Suppliers and use Add a supplier. For a UK company, enter its Companies House number. The register is checked as soon as the number is complete, and you see whether the company is active.
  2. Open the supplier to see its Supplier screening. It checks the company status, annual accounts, confirmation statement, officer changes and changes to people with significant control in the last 12 months, and runs a sanctions check.
  3. Read each result. Nothing found means the check found nothing to look at. For your review means something needs your attention. Use Open the Companies House record to read the source.
  4. Choose Run again before a decision if the last check is old.

When screening runs

Screening runs by itself when a supplier’s response arrives or when the supplier is added to an evaluation. It is not a score, and it never excludes a supplier. Your organisation makes that decision and records why.

After award

The supplier record holds the tabs for managing the contract: commitments, scorecards, concerns, risk, reviews and benefits. The directory shows each supplier’s contracts and a delivery track record taken from the scorecards you publish. The guide on managing the contract explains each tab.

Common problems

  • Companies House has no company with that number. Check the number. A UK company number is 8 characters, for example 01234567 or SC123456.
  • Companies House could not be checked just now. Enter the details by hand and run the screening again later.
  • The company is not active. The supplier record says so. Check with the supplier before you rely on them.

articles.title: Score bids with a panel and agree the final marks
articles.summary: Let each evaluator score on their own, compare the marks, agree one mark the panel can explain, and keep the record for feedback and audit.
articles.html:
Why a panel scores on its own first

Fair scoring means each evaluator reads the bids and decides a mark before seeing anyone else’s. Then the panel compares, talks through big differences and agrees one mark with a reason. Public bodies need this record to explain an award under the Procurement Act 2023, and private buyers benefit from the same discipline.

Step by step

  1. Open the evaluation from Evaluations and find Score with your panel.
  2. Under Who is on the panel, choose Choose the panel and mark each person as someone who Scores bids or the moderator who Agrees final marks. With no panel set, anyone in your team who can edit can score, and an owner or admin agrees the final marks.
  3. Each evaluator gives every bid a mark from 0 to 100 on each criterion, writes why, and chooses Submit my marks. A draft can be saved first. Only its author sees it.
  4. Show passages from this bid lists parts of the bid that may relate to a criterion. AI finds them to save reading time. It does not score. The evaluator decides the mark and writes the reason.

Agreeing the final marks

Under Agree the final marks, the moderator sees each evaluator’s mark and the difference between the highest and lowest. A large difference is flagged so the panel talks it through first. The moderator then saves the agreed mark and why the panel agreed it.

Check the reasons for consistency asks AI to point out where the written reasons do not match the marks. It does not score or rank. The moderator decides.

Scoring bands

The scoring bands and their descriptors are set when the requirement pack is built, and locked with the weightings when it is published. Every evaluator reads a mark the same way.

What happens next

Send the evaluation to moderation, then mark it complete, which locks every score. From the ranking you can prepare an assessment summary for each bidder, and draft award and regret letters, which you check and approve before sending.

Common problems

  • You cannot submit. Every bid needs a mark and a reason on every criterion first.
  • Panel scoring is not switched on. You can still score each bid on the evaluation.

articles.title: Set up your Velstrian Buy workspace and buyer profile
articles.summary: Tell us what kind of organisation is buying, where you buy and in what currency, so the right rules reach every requirement.
articles.html:
Who this is for

Anyone setting up Velstrian Buy for a public body or a private company. The answers here decide which procurement rules apply to every requirement you build.

1. Record what kind of organisation you are

Your organisation type is the fact every later step reads. A council, an NHS body, a school or a university is a public buyer. A company is a private buyer. Set it when you set up your organisation, or later in Settings, Organisation, General. Only an owner or an admin can record it, because it is a fact about the organisation.

Until it is recorded, the requirement builder shows Not recorded yet under Who is buying. Nothing is enforced and nothing is hidden until you answer, and any threshold shown is marked as assumed.

2. Record where you buy

In the same settings page, Jurisdiction records which nation's procurement rules your organisation buys under. It decides which statutory route and duties apply to an award. Leave it unanswered and the product says so rather than assuming one.

3. Set your market and default currency

Market is the country you trade from. Default currency is the currency a new private requirement starts in. Both are preselections you can change on each value. Stored values are never converted.

4. Add your local priorities (public buyers)

In Settings, Products, Velstrian Buy settings, add the outcomes your organisation cares about, each with a social value theme, an area or locality and a weight hint. You attach them to requirements later. The same page shows your tenancy tier, data region and isolation for reference.

What changes between public and private

  • A public buyer sees the Procurement Act 2023 threshold check, the sourcing routes and the social value steps.
  • A private buyer records the document being issued (an RFI, RFP, RFQ or invitation to tender) and an estimated value in its own currency, and social value measures are optional.

articles.title: Build a requirement, from a document or from blank
articles.summary: Start a requirement pack from a draft specification, last year's pack or a business case, or fill it in yourself.
articles.html:
Start a requirement

Go to Requirements and choose New requirement. The builder asks How do you want to start?

  • Start from a document. Upload a draft specification, last year's tender pack or a business case. We read what the document states and suggest a value for each field.
  • Start blank. Fill in every field yourself.

Checking what was read

Each suggestion shows the file and page it was read from. You accept, edit or reject each one, and every decision is recorded with your name. Names, references and dates can be accepted together. Figures, criteria and lots are checked one at a time. Anything not found is listed under Not found in this document for you to fill in. Nothing read from a document is a score.

A figure stated in another currency is not put into a pounds field and is never converted. A scanned document with no text cannot be read, so upload a text copy or type the details.

The first step: contract type and value

  • Give the requirement a name and choose the contract type and value band.
  • Public buyers answer What are you buying? (goods or services, or works) and the estimated total value including VAT, and see which side of the Procurement Act 2023 threshold it falls.
  • Choose the sourcing route you are running. You can change it until bids are submitted.
  • On the non statutory route, record the document you are issuing and, for a private purchase, the estimated value with its currency and tax basis.

Common problems

  • The value band is empty. It is worked out from the estimated value you enter, so enter that first.
  • Who is buying says Not recorded yet. Record your organisation type in settings so the right rules apply.

articles.title: Local priorities and social value measures (public buyers)
articles.summary: Attach the outcomes your organisation cares about, then choose the social value measures the contract should deliver.
articles.html:
Local priorities

The second step lists the local priorities recorded in your Velstrian Buy settings. Select the ones this contract should advance. With none recorded you can continue and add them later.

Social value measures

The third step offers measures from the social value measure library. When you open it, AI suggests measures for this contract. The suggestion is advisory: check each measure fits before you keep it, or run the suggestion again, or pick measures yourself if AI is unavailable.

The rail shows an estimated social value for the measures you chose. It is calculated from quantities fixed by the contract's value band, so set the value band first.

When measures are required

For a public buyer at least one measure must be chosen before you can continue. For a private buyer measures are optional, because no procurement rule asks a private company for them.

Step by step: add a local priority

  1. Open Settings, then Velstrian Buy settings, and find Local priorities.
  2. Under Add a local priority, give it a name, choose its social value theme, and say which area or locality it applies to.
  3. Add a weight hint, to show how much it matters, and choose Add priority.

Write priorities in plain words a supplier will understand, for example “jobs for young people in the borough” rather than a strategy reference.

What happens next

Each new requirement lists your priorities in its second step, so you pick the ones this contract should advance. The measures you choose in the third step are published with the pack, so suppliers know what you will score. After award, the commitments the winning supplier made are attached to the contract and tracked.

Common problems

  • No local priorities defined yet. You can continue without them and add them later in Velstrian Buy settings.
  • The estimated social value looks wrong. It depends on the value band, which is worked out from the estimated value in the first step. Check that value first.
  • The AI suggestion is unavailable. Pick the measures yourself, or choose Re-run AI suggestion later.

articles.title: Set the award weightings and scoring bands
articles.summary: Enter price, quality and social value weightings from your tender notice, and see the minimum that applies to your organisation.
articles.html:
Award criteria weightings

Enter the weightings from your own tender notice: price, quality and social value. They must total 100 percent before you can continue. These are published with the pack and are the weightings applied when bids are ranked.

Quality

Quality is scored by your evaluation panel as one consensus score on each bid. It is applied only when every bid in the tender has one. Until then it is shown as suspended and weighted at zero, and the evaluation says why.

The social value minimum

The builder tells you which minimum applies to your organisation, if any:

  • Required. A minimum your organisation must meet, with the instrument that sets it.
  • Guidance. You may publish below it, and you record why. The reason is stored on the published pack.
  • None. No UK procurement rule sets a weighting for your organisation.
  • Not recorded. We do not yet know what kind of organisation you are, so nothing is enforced.

Where it applies, the builder also says your organisation must obtain a Carbon Reduction Plan from suppliers.

Scoring bands

Each band carries a descriptor so every evaluator reads a mark the same way. The bands are locked with the weightings at publication.

What happens next

The weightings, the award criteria and the scoring bands are published with the pack and locked. When you open an evaluation against it, the award ranking applies these weightings and says which weighting is in force.

Common problems

  • The total is not 100%. Price, quality and social value must total 100% before you can continue.
  • The minimum says Not recorded. Record your organisation type in Settings, Organisation, General, so the right minimum applies.
  • You need to change a weighting after publishing. The weightings are locked at publication. Every evaluation checks them against the lock and reports any change, so decide them before you publish.

articles.title: Publish, download and share the requirement pack
articles.summary: Preview the pack, lock the weightings at publication, then download it as PDF or Word to send to suppliers.
articles.html:
Preview and publish

The last step previews the pack: contract type, value band, weightings, local priorities, the measures with their estimated values, and the submission instructions. Publish requirement pack saves it and takes the weight lock.

The requirement narrative

Below the preview you can draft a requirement narrative with AI or write your own. A draft is not part of the published pack until you approve it, and suppliers never see a draft. The figures are checked again when you publish, and the approval is recorded against your name.

Market sounding

The same step offers a market sounding from the published award record: enter a CPV code to see who won comparable contracts, how many bids those tenders drew and the published values. It is free and uses no AI.

What the weight lock does

At publication the price, quality and social value weightings, the award criteria and the scoring bands are hashed and timestamped, before any bid is received. Every evaluation against the pack checks them against that lock and reports any change.

Sharing the pack with suppliers

Publishing records the pack. It does not email suppliers. Open the requirement and use Download PDF or Word (.docx), then send the pack through your usual channel, such as your tendering portal or email.

After publishing

  • A change to an approved narrative is issued as a clarification or an addendum, with a reason every bidder reads in the pack.
  • Withdraw to draft or Archive changes how the pack reads on the register. Neither changes the locked weightings, the digest or the timestamp.

Common problems

  • Suppliers did not receive the pack. Publishing does not send anything. Download it and send it yourself.
  • The narrative is missing from the pack. A draft is only included once you approve it.

articles.title: Record suppliers in your directory
articles.summary: Add the suppliers you buy from, check them on Companies House, and see their contracts and delivery track record.
articles.html:
Add a supplier

Go to Suppliers and use Add a supplier. Enter the supplier name and, for a UK company, the Companies House number. Check on Companies House confirms the number before you save. A number already in your directory is refused, so open the existing supplier instead.

Why the directory matters

An evaluation adds bids from this directory, so record each bidder here before you score. Awarded contracts are linked to the supplier, and the directory shows each supplier's contracts and delivery track record.

The supplier record

Open a supplier to see its record and the tabs used to manage the relationship after award: commitments, scorecards, concerns, risk, reviews and benefits. The guide on managing the contract covers each one.

Step by step

  1. Open Suppliers and choose Add a supplier.
  2. Enter the supplier name. For a UK company, add the Companies House number and wait for the register check to say whether it is active.
  3. Add a contact email if you have one, then choose Add supplier.

You can also add a supplier while you build a comparison or normalise supplier prices, with Add a supplier who is not in your directory. It goes straight into the directory.

Finding a supplier later

Search by name, company number or email, and sort by name, most contracts or highest track record. Export CSV downloads the directory with each supplier’s contracts and delivery track record. The track record comes from the scorecards you publish, so a new supplier shows No published scorecard until you score one.

Common problems

  • A UK company number is 8 characters. For example 01234567 or SC123456.
  • Companies House could not be checked. Enter the supplier’s details by hand, or try again shortly.
  • The company is not active on the register. Check with the supplier before you record them.

articles.title: Open and run an evaluation, with the AI pre-read and consistency check
articles.summary: Score each bid against the published pack. The AI helps you read and checks consistency, and never sets or changes a score.
articles.html:
Open an evaluation

Go to Evaluations, pick a published requirement and, if it has one, a tender reference, then choose Open evaluation. Add a supplier bid for each supplier in your directory that responded.

Score each bid

  • Score each social value measure from 0 to 100.
  • Enter the tendered price, which is the price axis of the award ranking.
  • Enter the panel's consensus quality score from 0 to 100. It is never generated by AI and never derived from the social value score.

A bid missing a figure on a weighted criterion is held out of the ranking rather than scored zero, because a missing figure is an unread bid, not a poor one.

The AI pre-read

For each response you can generate a pre-read. It locates evidence in the supplier's response against each published criterion and quotes it word for word, lists what is not obviously addressed, and never scores, ranks or recommends a mark. A quote is only shown when it can be found in the response. If the pre-read is unavailable, read the response yourself and score as normal. Nothing is blocked.

The AI consistency check

Run consistency check comments on how consistently the panel has scored and what evidence it relied on. It is advisory and never changes a score. When AI is unavailable, or its draft is rejected, a rule based check runs instead and says so.

Limits to keep in mind

  • The panel evaluates and scores every response. The AI is a reading aid.
  • The weightings are checked against the lock taken at publication, and any change is reported above the ranking.
  • Move the evaluation on with Send to moderation and Mark complete.

articles.title: Compare bids, whole life cost and bid normalisation
articles.summary: Lay options side by side, cost each way of delivering a requirement over its whole life, and put supplier prices on one footing.
articles.html:
Comparisons

A comparison holds the options you are weighing up as columns, your criteria as rows, and the judgement a named person made in each cell. New comparison takes three steps: the segment (a CPV code, or none), what goes in (bids received against an evaluation, registered suppliers, options added by hand or market options), and the criteria you weight.

Whole life cost models

In Whole life costs, a model holds each way you could deliver a requirement and what each would cost across the term. You state the term, the price base year and the discounting: the HM Treasury Green Book rate, a rate your organisation states, or none. Nothing is filled in for you, because a figure resting on an assumption you did not make is not your figure.

Bid normalisation

From Whole life costs, Normalise supplier prices turns each supplier's price schedule into one whole life figure over the same term and quantities. Price lines can be one off, per year or per unit. Present value with Green Book rates is optional. Bids in different currencies are shown in separate groups and are never compared or converted.

When to use each one

  • Use a comparison when you need to set out why you prefer one option, for example for a business case or a board paper.
  • Use a whole life cost model before you go to market, to see whether buying, leasing or a service contract costs less over the term.
  • Use bid normalisation when suppliers price in different ways, so you compare like with like.

Common problems

  • A price has more decimal places than its currency uses. Nothing is rounded for you, so check the figure the supplier sent.
  • A supplier priced in another currency. Their figure is shown in its own group and never converted. Ask for a price in your currency if you need to compare them directly.
  • A model is empty. Every assumption is yours to enter. Nothing is filled in for you.

articles.title: Award a contract: standstill for public buyers, letters for every bidder
articles.summary: Award from the ranking, see the standstill that applies to a public buyer, and draft award and regret letters.
articles.html:
Before you award

Award is available only when every bid on the evaluation is complete. If bids are level on score, social value and price, the evaluation says so. Resolve the tie before you award.

Award and create the contract

Award & create contract on the winning row creates the contract at once, with the social value commitments from the winning bid attached, and takes you to Contracts. Check the ranking before you select it.

Standstill (public buyers)

For a contracting authority, the contracts list shows when the mandatory standstill under the Procurement Act 2023 ends, counted in working days from the award date, with a note on how bank holidays were treated. Do not enter the contract before that date.

A private buyer owes no standstill, and the contracts list says so.

Award and regret letters

The evaluation can draft an award letter for the winner and a regret letter for each other bidder. Drafts are advisory and are not legal advice. Your organisation reviews and approves each letter before sending it. If AI drafting is unavailable, or a draft states a figure, date or period that was not supplied, a standard template letter is shown instead.

Assessment summaries (public buyers)

Under the Procurement Act 2023 each bidder whose tender was assessed is owed a summary of its own assessment. Choose Prepare assessment summaries on the evaluation. Replace each placeholder in brackets, check the passages that are redacted by default, then choose Approve this summary and copy or download it to send. The summaries are drafts built from your records and are not legal advice.

Common problems

  • Award is unavailable. A bid on the evaluation is not complete. Finish scoring it, or save the scores you entered, first.
  • Letters cannot be drafted yet. They can be drafted once every bid can be ranked.

articles.title: Manage the contract, commitments and supplier reviews
articles.summary: Record contracts, confirm what the supplier promised, score delivery and run review meetings.
articles.html:
Contracts

An awarded evaluation creates its contract. To add one awarded elsewhere, use Record a contract on Contracts, or Start from the signed contract: we read the title, value and dates it states and you decide what goes into the form.

The supplier's tabs

Open the supplier from Suppliers to manage the relationship:

  • Commitments. Every promise from the supplier's winning bids. Confirm each one to add it to the ledger the supplier is measured against. KPIs and commitments can also be read from the signed contract, as proposals for you to confirm.
  • Scorecards. Score the supplier for each period and choose which scorecards are released to them.
  • Concerns. Concerns raised, the corrective action plans put in place, and commendations.
  • Risk. What the platform has worked out from its own records, and what your team has flagged, kept apart.
  • Reviews. Monthly and quarterly review sessions, with their packs, sealed minutes and signatures.
  • Benefits. Savings and other value claimed against the supplier, and what finance has signed off.

Step by step

  1. Open Commitments and confirm each promise from the winning bid, so it joins the ledger the supplier is measured against.
  2. Schedule a monthly or quarterly review on Reviews, and record what was agreed.
  3. At the end of each period, score the supplier on Scorecards and choose whether to release the scorecard to them.
  4. Record any problem on Concerns, with the corrective action plan agreed, and record good work as a commendation.

What happens next

Published scorecards build the supplier’s delivery track record, which the supplier directory shows beside their name. That record helps the next time you choose a supplier.

Common problems

  • No commitments recorded yet. Record the promises from the supplier’s winning bid so they can be confirmed and then tracked.
  • A scorecard is missing from the track record. Only published scorecards count, so publish it first.

articles.title: Quick RFQ for private sector buyers
articles.summary: Describe a job or upload what you have, check the scope, then download an RFQ pack and a price schedule for suppliers.
articles.html:
When to use it

Quick RFQ is the short route for a private sector purchase with a settled scope, when you want prices back quickly without building a full requirement pack.

1. Start

Choose Describe the job and say what you need, where, by when and how much of it, or Upload what you have (PDF, DOCX or TXT). Your organisation's default currency is chosen for you and amounts are never converted. Set the response and questions deadlines.

2. Review

AI drafts the scope only. It never writes a price, a rate or a term. Each scope item shows where it came from, and you accept, change or remove it. A suggestion whose words could not be found in your brief or document is left out and counted. The price schedule lines carry a description, quantity and unit, with no rate column, because suppliers price them.

Write the timetable and submission instructions yourself, and attach one of your organisation's saved terms templates or choose no terms. Velstrian Tenderworks never writes or suggests terms. Templates are kept in Settings, Products, Velstrian Buy settings, Terms templates.

3. Export

Decide every AI suggestion and choose the terms, then download the RFQ pack (Word or PDF) and the price schedule (Excel). Only accepted and edited items are exported.

4. Send to suppliers

Send the RFQ through the invite step. Each supplier gets a personal link to the RFQ, uploads a quote and gets a receipt, and the quote lands on the evaluation. Your recent requests for quotation are listed with how many quotes are back.

Common problems

  • The brief is too short. Write enough to draft a scope from: what you need, where, by when and how much of it.
  • No terms to choose from. Add your terms templates in Settings first, or choose no terms.

articles.title: Bid to a private sector buyer
articles.summary: Start a bid for a commercial buyer, and see what the workspace keeps and leaves off when no procurement statute applies.
articles.html:
Choose who you are bidding to

Choose Start a bid. The first question is Who are you bidding to? Choose Private sector for a commercial buyer running its own process through an RFI, RFP, RFQ or invitation to tender. No procurement statute applies. You can change the answer before the bid is created.

How the bid starts

Drop the RFP, RFQ or invitation pack, the specification and the pricing schedule, or enter the details yourself. Two starting points are not offered for a private bid: Discover lists tenders published by public buyers, and a framework call off is a public procurement route.

What a private bid records

  • The buyer's country, preselected from your organisation's market.
  • The time zone the deadline is stated in. A deadline is never saved without its zone.
  • The value with its own currency. Values are never converted.
  • Every country or region the contract covers.

What the workspace keeps

The documents, requirements, answers, review and submission screens. It leaves off the tools that only UK public procurement law requires: social value, statutory KPIs and the selection questionnaire.

What happens next

The bid opens on Tender, where you confirm the requirements read from the buyer’s documents. Then answer the questions on Response, review on Sign-off, and download your response with Export. You send it to the buyer yourself, then record the result on Submit and outcome. If the buyer only wants prices, Quick quote is faster.

Common problems

  • The deadline will not save. Choose the time zone the deadline is stated in. A deadline is never saved without its zone.
  • The value is in another currency. Choose the buyer’s currency on the bid. Nothing is converted.
  • You chose public by mistake. Change the answer to Who are you bidding to? before you create the bid.

articles.title: Set your market and default currency
articles.summary: Tell Velstrian Bid which country you trade from and which currency new values start in, without changing any public sector rule.
articles.html:
Market

Market is the country your organisation trades from. It sets the tax and identifier labels and the defaults for private bids, such as the buyer’s country. It never changes which procurement rules apply to a public bid. With no market saved, one is suggested from your address country, and nothing is stored until you save.

Default currency

Default currency is the currency a new value starts in, for example a private bid, a private requirement, a quick quote or a Quick RFQ. It is a preselection you can change on each value. Velstrian Bid never converts a stored value, and this is not the currency you are billed in.

Where to set them

Both are asked when you set up your organisation, and can be changed at any time in Settings, Organisation, General by an owner or an admin. A Companies House lookup on the same page fills the name, number and address for a UK company.

Step by step

  1. Open Settings, then General in the Organisation part.
  2. Check Market. If it says it was suggested from your address country, check it and save to confirm it.
  3. Choose your Default currency and save.

What happens next

New private bids, quotes and requirements start in your market and currency. Values you already saved keep the currency they were saved in. If you bid for work abroad, change the currency on that bid only. Values are never converted from one currency to another.

A setting that is easy to confuse

Tender markets, in Velstrian Bid settings, chooses which markets your opportunity search and alerts cover, UK and EU by default. It does not change your organisation’s market.

Common problems

  • You cannot change these fields. Only an owner or an admin can, because they are facts about the organisation.
  • A value shows the wrong currency. Change the currency on that value. The default only applies to new values.

articles.title: Price a quote for a private buyer with Quick Quote
articles.summary: Turn a buyer's request into a priced quotation, one line at a time, in the buyer's currency.
articles.html:
Start

Open Quick quote. Paste or describe the buyer's request, or upload the buyer's RFQ (PDF, DOCX or XLSX). A Quick RFQ price schedule is read without AI. Name the buyer, choose the currency and check the valid until date, which is 30 days from today unless you change it.

Velstrian Bid keeps every quote on a bid, so you also give the sector, where the work is delivered, the expected value and the duration. These answers are yours and are never filled in for you.

Review and price

AI restates the scope only. It never writes a price, a rate or a term. Accept, change or remove each scope item, then enter a unit rate on each line, typed or taken from your rate card. Totals are shown per currency, with the VAT rate you enter. Amounts in different currencies are never added together or converted.

Cover note, terms and export

A cover note can be drafted from the scope you accepted. It never holds a number and is yours to edit. Attach one of your saved supplier quote terms or choose no terms, then download the quotation.

What happens next

Send the quotation to the buyer yourself, by email or through their portal. The quote stays on its bid, so you can record the result when you hear back. Rates you use often can be kept in your Rate card in Velstrian Bid settings, and your quote terms in Terms templates.

Common problems

  • That file type cannot be read here. Use a PDF, DOCX or XLSX file, or paste the request.
  • Things need your attention before the draft can start. The list names each one, such as the buyer or the currency.

articles.title: Run a private sector purchase in Velstrian Buy
articles.summary: What changes for a private company buying: the document you issue, your own currency, optional social value and no statutory standstill.
articles.html:
How the product knows you are a private buyer

From your recorded organisation type. A company is a private buyer, and the requirement builder shows it under Who is buying. Until the type is recorded nothing is enforced and nothing is hidden.

Building a requirement

  • Choose the non statutory route and record the document you are issuing: a request for information, a request for proposal, a request for quotation or an invitation to tender.
  • Enter the estimated value in the currency you are buying in, preselected from your default currency. It is stored with its currency and never converted.
  • Social value measures are optional, because no procurement rule asks a private company for them.
  • No UK procurement rule sets a social value weighting for you. Set whatever your own policy requires.

Awarding

No standstill applies to a private buyer, so you are free to enter the contract when you are ready. Award and regret letters are still drafted for you to review.

The short route

For a settled scope, Quick RFQ produces an RFQ pack and a price schedule without a full requirement pack. See the Quick RFQ guide.

What happens next

When you award from the ranking, the contract appears on Contracts with the commitments from the winning bid attached, and the list says that no standstill applies. Manage the supplier from Suppliers: confirm what they promised, score each period and run reviews.

Common problems

  • The builder shows public sector steps. Your organisation type is not recorded as a company. An owner or admin can record it in Settings, Organisation, General.
  • A value shows the wrong currency. Choose the currency on that value. Your default currency only preselects it.
  • You want to compare supplier prices. Use bid normalisation in Whole life costs. Prices in different currencies are shown in separate groups and never converted.

articles.title: Enterprise Single Sign-On (SAML 2.0) & SCIM directory sync
articles.summary: Let your team sign in with Microsoft, Google, Okta or another identity provider, and add or remove people automatically.
articles.html:
Do you need this?

Most small teams do not. Two-factor authentication and the organisation security policy are enough. Single sign-on (SSO) is for organisations that already run their own sign-in service, such as Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace or Okta, and want everyone to sign in to Velstrian Tenderworks the same way. SCIM lets that service add and remove people for you. Both work with any identity provider that supports SAML 2.0 and SCIM 2.0.

Before you start

You need to be an owner or an admin, and you need someone who can change settings in your identity provider. Everything below is in Settings, then Authentication.

Step 1: verify your email domain

  1. Open Domain verification, enter your domain and choose Generate TXT record.
  2. Add that TXT record to your domain’s DNS, then choose Check.

This is only needed if you will require single sign-on.

Step 2: connect SAML single sign-on

  1. In SAML single sign-on, copy the ACS URL and the SP Entity ID into a new SAML app in your identity provider.
  2. Paste your identity provider’s metadata XML and choose Fill from XML, or paste its metadata URL and choose Fetch and fill. You can also type the IdP Entity ID, IdP SSO URL and signing certificate yourself.
  3. Choose the Default role for new users, and whether new users are created on their first sign-in.
  4. Tick Enable this connection and choose Save connection.
  5. When it works, you can turn on Require SSO, which blocks password sign-in for your verified domains.

Step 3: turn on SCIM (optional)

In SCIM directory provisioning, choose Generate token and copy it straight away, because it is shown only once. Put the base URL and the token into your identity provider’s SCIM settings. People are then added and removed as you change them there.

Common problems

  • That document is not identity provider metadata. Use the metadata of your SAML app in the identity provider, not the Velstrian Tenderworks metadata.
  • The metadata has no signing certificate. Paste the certificate into its own field instead.
  • Removing the connection stops sign-in through your identity provider straight away. People keep their accounts.

articles.title: Plans, billing and invoices
articles.summary: Choose a plan, add users, check your monthly AI credits and download your invoices.
articles.html:
Velstrian Tenderworks plans

There is a plan for a one person business writing its own bids and for a bigger team bidding every week, whether you sell to public sector or private sector buyers. Every plan is self serve: choose it in Settings > Billing and it starts straight away. Prices are in pounds sterling.

Velstrian Bid plans
