AI credits explained

One AI credit corresponds to one full generation of an answer narrative. Compliance matrix parsing, TOMs scoring calculations, document viewing, and standard exports do not consume AI credits.

Subscription management

Account owners change plan, or add users where the plan allows it, in Settings > Billing.

The page opens on your plan and its one main action, for example Upgrade to Pro on Starter. A move up starts today and you pay the difference for the rest of the period. A move down takes effect at the end of the period you have paid for.

One control on that page opens the Stripe billing portal: Invoices and card details, in the Payment and invoices section. Payment method, billing address, tax IDs and the full invoice history are all there. Invoices are also reachable from the Invoices row in the settings menu, which opens the same portal.

articles.title: Invite your team and choose what each person can do
articles.summary: Add colleagues, give each person the right role (Admin, Manager, Viewer or Billing-Only), and manage your seats.
articles.html:
Who this is for

The owner or an admin of an organisation. A bid is easier with help, so you can invite colleagues and choose what each person can see and change. People you invite use the seats your plan includes.

The roles

Role What they can do
Owner Everything, including transferring ownership. There is one owner.
Admin Everything a Manager can do, plus inviting, changing roles for and removing members, and managing billing, plans and organisation settings.
Manager Full day to day work: create and edit bids, answers, requirements and reports, draft answers, run evaluations and export. Cannot manage the team, billing or settings.
Viewer Reads everything, comments on answers and records an approve, changes requested or reject decision on a bid. Cannot create, edit, export or delete.
Billing-Only Manages plans, payment methods and invoices, with no access to bids or reports.

The page also shows a full list of what each role can do, under What each role can do.

Step by step

  1. Open Settings, then Members & access.
  2. Under Invite a team member, enter one email address, or several separated by commas or new lines.
  3. Choose a role and select Send invite. For your security you may be asked for a fresh code from your authenticator first.

What happens next

Each person gets an email invitation and shows as Invite pending, with the time left before it expires. When they accept, they appear as Active. To change the role of a pending invitation, revoke it and invite again. To take someone off the team, choose Remove. They lose access straight away.

Common problems

  • Seat limit reached. All your seats are in use. Remove a member, or upgrade or add seats on the Billing page.
  • Already a member. That address already belongs to the team or has a pending invitation.
  • Someone outside your organisation needs to read one bid. Invite them as an external reviewer on that bid’s Sign-off stage instead. Your plan lists how many guest reviewers it includes.

articles.title: Security baselines, MFA enforcement, recovery codes & data controls
articles.summary: Turn on two-factor authentication, add a passkey, keep your recovery codes safe, set sign-in rules for your organisation and download a copy of your data.
articles.html:
Who this is for

Everyone with an account. Bids hold prices, plans and staff details a competitor would like to see, so a few minutes here protects your work. The organisation rules further down are for the owner or an admin.

Protect your own account

Open Settings, then Sign-in & security. It lists your password, two-factor authentication, passkeys, recovery codes, trusted devices and active sessions.

  1. Turn on two-factor authentication. Choose Enable two-factor authentication, scan the QR code with an authenticator app such as Google Authenticator, 1Password or Authy, then enter the 6-digit code. It is required for the Owner and Admin roles.
  2. Save your recovery codes somewhere safe. Each code works once, and they let you in if you lose your phone.
  3. Add a passkey if you like, so you sign in with your face, fingerprint or screen lock instead of typing a password.
  4. Check your active sessions and sign out any device you do not recognise.

Set rules for your organisation

Owners and admins open Authentication in the Organisation part of Settings. The organisation security policy can:

  • require two-factor authentication for every member,
  • set a minimum password length and the character types a password needs,
  • sign members out after a period of inactivity, from 15 minutes up to 7 days,
  • turn off the 30 day “Remember me” sign-in.

The same page holds an IP allowlist, which limits access to the addresses you approve, and says whether your plan includes it. Single sign-on is there too, for organisations that sign in with Microsoft, Google or Okta.

Get a copy of your data

In Preferences & privacy, choose Go to Your data, then Request export. You confirm it is you with your second factor first. We prepare a full copy of the records we hold on your account and email you a private download link, usually within a few minutes. The export history shows each request and when its link expires.

Common problems

  • Lost your authenticator? Sign in with a recovery code. If you have lost the codes too, Sign-in & security explains how to reset two-factor authentication.
  • Asked to verify again? Some actions, such as inviting a colleague or exporting data, ask for a fresh code from your authenticator first. Enter it and carry on.
  • Few recovery codes left? Regenerate a fresh set so you are not locked out.

articles.title: See who did what in the audit log
articles.summary: See sign-ins, team changes, billing changes and bid activity in one record, filter it, and export a copy for your own files.
articles.html:
What the audit log is for

The audit log records who did what, and when, across your organisation. It helps when a buyer or your insurer asks how you control access to your data, when you need to check who changed a bid, or when something looks wrong and you want to see what happened.

What it records

  • Sign-in and security: sign-ins, failed sign-ins, two-factor authentication turned on or off, passkeys added, password changes and sessions signed out.
  • Your team: invitations sent, accepted and revoked, role changes, members removed and ownership transferred.
  • Billing: plan changes, payments and cancellations.
  • Bids: tender documents added or removed, requirements confirmed or changed, compliance matrix updates and evidence removed.
  • Your data: requests for a copy of personal data, and account or organisation deletions.

Step by step

  1. Open Settings, then Audit log in the Organisation part. Owners and admins can see it.
  2. Filter by Action, by User and by date with From and To.
  3. Choose View on any row to see the full detail, including the request ID.
  4. Choose Export CSV or Export JSON to download the events that match your filters.

Times are shown in UTC, and the newest events come first.

Keeping your own copy

We keep this record for 24 months from the date of each event. If you need it for longer, for example for a contract that runs several years, export a copy and keep it in your own files.

Common problems

  • No events match these filters. Try a wider date range, or clear the action and user filters.
  • The export holds only the most recent events. Very large exports are capped. Narrow the date range and export again to reach older events.
  • We couldn’t load the audit log. This is a loading problem, not an empty log. Choose Refresh to try again.

articles.title: How to get help, report a problem or book a call
articles.summary: Choose the quickest way to get help, see when our team is available, and report a problem so it can be fixed fast.
articles.html:
Four ways to get help

Open Help and support from the menu. Pick the route that suits your question.

Route Best for When
AI support assistant How to questions and quick answers about Velstrian Tenderworks, procurement and social value. Any time it shows as available.
Report an issue Something that is not working. Any time. You get a reference straight away.
Email us at contact@velstrian.com Account, billing and detailed questions. We’ll reply by email, usually within one business day.
Book a call A walkthrough or a longer conversation. A 30 minute call at a time you choose.

Asking the assistant

Select Help and support (the lifebuoy icon) in the top bar, or Help in the menu on a phone, then Ask the AI support assistant. General questions are answered without using your data. To get answers about your own bids and account, turn on AI data consent in Preferences & privacy first. You can turn it off at any time.

Talking to a person

Our support team works Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 18:00 UK time. In those hours you can start a live chat with the team. At any other time, leave a message from the same panel and we reply by email.

Reporting a problem well

  1. Choose Report an issue, then Start report.
  2. Say what you were trying to do, what you expected and what happened instead.
  3. Send it. We attach your request ID, the page, your browser, window size and time zone, so support can find your session without asking you for them.

If you reached support from an error page, the request ID from that error is included for you.

Common problems

  • The booking calendar does not load. A browser extension or network block can stop it. Use the link to open the calendar in a new tab.
  • The assistant shows as offline. Email us instead, or report the issue.
